title: Promote comparative findings only after checking real callers and maturity
summary: Pinned upstream code, tests and local call paths support a scoped adoption hypothesis; they do not prove exploitability, production maturity or performance improvement.
reusable_steps: Pinned upstream code, tests and local call paths support a scoped adoption hypothesis; they do not prove exploitability, production maturity or performance improvement
expected_outcome: For comparative agent research, pin the upstream source and identify the local checkout and uncommitted boundary inspected. Trace helpers into actual callers and inspect counterexamples before claiming that a capability is absent or fully deployed. An upstream contract or test can justify a fail-closed design without proving that a production provider implements it. Preserve the distinction between static findings, executed regressions, service-level measurements and permission to publish. Prefer extending existing WorkItems, journals, alerts, approval facades and comparison harnesses instead of adding parallel state stores. Keep passive freshness and advisory knowledge relations separate from authorization and completion gates. Prioritize bounded defenses and explicit outcome contracts before larger shared-context changes. Defer input queues, advisory graphs and optional multi-model features until measured demand and scope, delivery and cost contracts exist. A passing test count or upstream benchmark is not evidence of local long-running reliability, actual cost reduction or a confirmed security exploit.
